#5339. Estate Planning Attorney Jennifer McKenna Addresses Whether You Need a Trust or if a Will Is Enough

Jennifer McKenna explains how trusts and wills work together to support an estate planning strategy based on individual needs.

LEE'S SUMMIT, Mo., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Do you need a trust or is a will enough? A HelloNation article featuring insights from Estate Planning Attorney Jennifer McKenna of the Jennifer Ward McKenna, Attorney at Law in Lees Summit, Missouri, explains how trusts and wills serve different purposes within an estate planning strategy.

The article explains that many people begin estate planning by asking whether they need a trust or a will. The answer depends on factors such as family circumstances, financial goals, the types of assets they own, and how they want those assets managed after death. The article notes that both legal tools play important roles and understanding their differences helps individuals make informed decisions.

According to the article, a will is a legal document that explains how a person's property should be distributed after death. It also allows someone to name an executor to manage the estate and nominate guardians for minor children when necessary. The article describes a will as the foundation of many estate planning plans because it provides clear instructions and guidance for loved ones during a difficult time.

The HelloNation article also explains that a will always goes through the probate process after death. During probate, the court validates the will, oversees the payment of debts, and authorizes the distribution of assets. While probate is a routine legal process, the article notes that the timeline depends on the amount of assets administered through the will, the complexity of the estate, and state law. Some estates move through probate relatively quickly, while most require several months to resolve legal or administrative matters.

A trust serves a different purpose by allowing assets to be managed by a trustee for the benefit of designated beneficiaries. Unlike a will, many assets held in a properly funded trust can pass directly to beneficiaries without going through probate. The article explains that avoiding probate is one of the primary reasons some individuals include a trust as part of an overall estate planning strategy. It also notes that a trust can provide instructions for managing assets if the person creating the trust becomes unable to manage financial matters during their lifetime or when a beneficiary is unable to manage an inheritance effectively, such as a young child or an individual with special needs.

The article emphasizes that a trust is not automatically the right choice for every family. Establishing and maintaining a trust requires additional planning, and assets must be properly transferred into the trust for it to function as intended. If assets remain outside the trust, they may still be subject to probate. The article explains that understanding how a trust works is just as important as deciding whether to create one.

Rather than viewing these documents as alternatives, the article explains that a will and a trust often work together. A trust may be used to manage significant assets, while a will can address property that was not transferred into the trust and nominate guardians for minor children. According to the article, this combination creates a more complete estate planning approach that reflects a family's specific circumstances and long-term goals.

The article also notes that every estate is different, and no single solution works for everyone. Some individuals focus on protecting young children, while others are more concerned with managing business interests, real estate, or investment accounts. Estate planning allows legal documents to reflect those priorities instead of relying on general assumptions.

The article concludes that delaying estate planning because of uncertainty about choosing a trust or a will can leave important questions unanswered. Learning how a trust, a will, and probate work allows individuals to make informed decisions that fit their own circumstances. Whether someone ultimately chooses a will, a trust, or both, taking time to understand these legal tools can provide greater clarity and help protect loved ones in the future.

Do You Need a Trust or Is a Will Enough? Features insights from Jennifer McKenna, Estate Planning Attorney of Lees Summit, Missouri, in HelloNation.

#5338. Wireless networking chip startup Altair nabs $100M investment

Altair Semiconductor Ltd., a supplier of wireless networking chips for connected devices, today announced that it has raised $100 million in funding.

Maverick Silicon led the Series A round. It was reportedly joined by Pitango, which invested $50 million in Altair when it spun out of Sony Corp. earlier this year. The Japanese electronics giant is said to have retained a stake.

Connected devices such as wearables and industrial sensors transmit their data traffic via the same carrier infrastructure as smartphones. However, they access that infrastructure in different ways. Connected devices using specialized, low-power network protocols to exchange data with each one and to upload readings to cloud-based backends.

Altair’s flagship modem chip, the ALT1550, supports several such protocols. The most advanced technology in the lineup is the 5G NR eRedCap protocol, which uses 5G networks to transmit data. It consumes significantly less power than a standard smartphone connection and can transmit up to 233 megabits per second.

The ALT1550 also supports two alternative protocols called LTE-M and Cat 1bis. Both use 4G network infrastructure, which is more widely available than the latest 5G hardware. LTE-M can process up to 1 megabits per second, while Cat 1bis is ten times faster and uses more power.

The chip combines a transceiver that picks up and generates radio signals with a baseband processor. That’s a chip specifically optimized for wireless networking tasks. It’s supported by an onboard memory pool, power management circuits and a module that can connect to a satellite when there’s no cell tower nearby.

The ALT1550 is one of several chips offered by Altair. An earlier module, the ALT1255, supports a network protocol called NB-IoT that uses even less power than LTE-M and Cat 1bis. It’s designed for devices that only transmit data every few weeks or months. The ALT1255 provides additional power savings by deactivating many of its features when it’s not in use.

Altair says that its silicon can be found in millions of devices. Utilities use it to power smart meters, which automatically transmit usage data to the cloud and thereby remove the need for manual readings. Delivery companies can use Altair chips to track the location of their trucks. The company’s modules also power medical devices, street lights and a wide range of other systems.

Altair will use its new funding round to kick off the mass production of its flagship ALT1550 chip. Additionally, the company plans to develop new networking products and grow its international presence.

Chase Home Lending is offering a limited-time mortgage rate discount of up to 0.25% for eligible purchase and refinance loans. Borrowers must lock a rate from Nov. 30 through Dec. 13, and discounts can pair with select programs.  AI Summary

Chase Home Lending is offering a limited-time mortgage rate discount for eligible home purchase and refinance loans as borrowers continue to search for affordability.

The promotion runs from Nov. 30 through Dec. 13. Qualified borrowers could receive a rate discount of up to 0.25%, depending on their location and loan type.

Existing and new Chase customers must qualify for a purchase or refinance loan and lock in their rate during the promotional period. The company said there are no additional criteria to qualify for the sale.

The rate discount can be combined with other available Chase Home Lending programs and discounts, subject to their terms and eligibility requirements. These include the Chase Homebuyer Grant and the bank’s Relationship Pricing Program, which recently expanded eligibility to more than 7 million small-business customers.

Maximum discounts and other limitations may apply depending on how the rate sale is combined with other programs, the company clarified.

November’s rate sale is not Chase’s first promotion this year.

In September, the lender offered qualified borrowers up to 0.25 percentage points off mortgage rates on purchase and refinance loans. The company also ran promotions in May, covering purchase and refinance loans, and in March, when it offered discounted rates on new purchase and refi loans.

#5335. Mortgage hires: Genworth names CEO, FHLB New York elects chair

Recent mortgage industry announcements include Genworth CEO Thomas McInerney stepping down and Jerome Upton taking over; Charles Kilbourne's election as FHLB New York board chair, Darrell Boan joining Element Home Loans in Greensboro, North Carolina; and Fannie Mae appointing David Shafer to its board and approving $4.75 million in executive retention awards.  AI Summary

Thomas J. McInerney, president and CEO of Genworth Financial, has stepped down from his roles at the company and its board of directors to focus on his health, the company announced. The board appointed Jerome T. Upton, its current chief financial officer, as president, CEO and director. Upton will remain CFO through Dec. 31, with Angela Simmons expected to assume the role on Jan. 1, 2027.

Fannie Mae appointed David Shafer to its board of directors effective Nov. 23. His term will end at the next annual board election, or if he resigns or is removed by the Federal Housing Finance Agency. His committee assignments have not yet been determined.

The company also entered into retention agreements with four executives totaling $4.75 million. Chief financial officer Chryssa Halley and chief investment officer Erik Bisso will each receive $1.5 million, multifamily executive vice president Kelly Follain will receive $1 million, and chief risk officer Anthony Moon will receive $750,000.

The awards will be paid in two equal installments, in December 2026 and December 2027, provided the executives remain employed and comply with the agreements, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The Federal Home Loan Bank of New York elected Charles E. Kilbourne, managing director of the Financial Services Volunteer Corps and an independent director since 2019, as board chair for a two-year term beginning Jan. 1, 2027. Kilbourne, who chairs the board’s housing committee, will succeed Chris Martin, who is retiring at the end of this year after more than a decade of service.

Element Home Loans, a division of NFM Lending, has hired Darrell Boan as branch manager in Greensboro, North Carolina, as the company expands its presence in the Southeast. Boan, who has more than 25 years of mortgage industry experience, will lead local growth, support loan originators, and build relationships with clients and community partners.

#5333. The referral source real estate agents overlook is sitting in the next office

A durable client pipeline can come from agent referral partners. Start with colleagues in your brokerage, then expand through events, committees and cross market relationships built on follow through.  AI Summary

I’ve spent more than 25 years in this business, and one pattern has held strong in every market I’ve worked in: the agents who build lasting careers rarely do it alone. They have a network of fellow agents who think of them first when a client needs help. At The Agency, we were built on that idea. We encourage our agents to reach across the aisle, even to competitors, because when agents collaborate, more deals get done and clients are better served.

Referrals between agents get less attention than they deserve. We talk constantly about our sphere of influence, past clients and social media. Yet a colleague who’s relocating a client to your market, or who’s overbooked and can’t take on a new listing, might hand you a deal worth far more than a month of lead generation. Those opportunities only come to agents who’ve earned a place in someone’s mind.

Your brokerage is the most natural place to begin, and it’s often the most overlooked. Most of us share an office, a leadership team and a set of tools with dozens or even hundreds of agents, and many of us barely know their names.

Introduce yourself. Show up at the sales meeting, the training and the broker open, and stay for the conversation afterward. Ask people what they specialize in, what kind of client they love working with, and what they’d happily hand off. You’ll learn who’s the go-to for condos, who knows the hillside neighborhoods best, and who’s the strongest negotiator in the building.

That knowledge pays off quickly. When a client mentions a need outside your expertise, you’ll know exactly who to call. When a colleague gets a request that fits your strengths, they’ll know to call you. Trust inside a brokerage builds slowly, but once it’s there, it makes everyone’s business stronger.

Competition is part of this industry, and I won’t pretend otherwise. But the agent across the street at another firm is also a potential partner, and the best ones treat them that way.

Think about how much of real estate is geographic. Clients move across the country, across the state, sometimes across town into a different market. Your client in Los Angeles who’s buying in Aspen needs someone they can trust on the ground, and you can’t be that person. A thoughtful agent in Aspen, whom you’ve met and vetted, can. The same goes in reverse. That’s a referral built on mutual respect, and it often leads to repeat business flowing both ways for years.

Industry events, local board committees and MLS involvement are all excellent places to meet these people. You see how people handle disagreement, how they treat staff, and how they follow through. That’s the kind of insight no online profile will give you.

If you want referrals, you have to be worth referring. When one agent sends a client to another, they’re putting their own reputation on the line. They want to know that their client will be taken care of, that communication will be prompt, and that the deal will be handled with integrity.

So treat every interaction with another agent as an audition, whether or not it’s a referral situation. Return calls quickly. Show up prepared. Be the person who makes a tough negotiation easier instead of harder. Agents remember who was gracious under pressure, and they remember who wasn’t.

Close the loop, too. If someone sends you a client, keep them updated and thank them, even when the deal takes months. It sounds small, but plenty of agents forget, and the ones who don’t stand out.

I’d encourage agents to build  a simple structure around this. Set a goal to connect with a few new agents each month, one or two inside your brokerage and a few outside it. Grab coffee or hop on a quick call. Send a note when you see a colleague’s listing go under contract. Ask how you can be useful before you ask for anything.

It doesn’t take much time, just consistency and a willingness to see other agents as allies. Your next client might be working with an agent down the hall right now, or with one in a brokerage across the country. Sooner or later, that client will ask for a recommendation. Make sure the agent who gets asked already knows you.

Rainy Hake Austin is a brokerage leader at The Agency.

#5330. SAP reportedly plans to lay off 10,000+ employees amid AI push

Enterprise software giant SAP SE is reportedly planning to lay off at least 10,000 employees, or more than 9% of its workforce.

Bloomberg today cited sources as saying that the scope of the restructuring initiative is still subject to change.

According to the publication, SAP and a labor council in its home country of Germany have negotiated an “employment guarantee” that will run through 2028. That may mean the layoffs will mainly affect employees in other markets. The report indicates that SAP’s product, engineering and sales units are expected to see the largest cuts.

Executives have reportedly also asked other departments to find cost reduction opportunities.

The reported restructuring push follows a banner quarter for SAP. The company’s sales and adjusted profit both topped analyst expectations. Its €24.11 billion cloud contract backlog, a measure of future revenue, also came in ahead of the consensus estimate.

The planned layoffs are said to be connected to SAP’s efforts to integrate more artificial intelligence features into its products. The company is best known for its ERP, or enterprise resource planning, software. Enterprises use it to automate a long list of backoffice tasks and share data between teams. SAP also sells cloud services for other use cases such as sales automation and customer support.

At a May user conference, the company introduced an AI interface called Joule Work for its applications. SAP says that the tool will enable workers to centrally access its products instead of navigating multiple screens.

Joule Work made its debut alongside a suite of AI agents dubbed Joule Assistants. According to SAP, they will use over 200 subagents to automate repetitive business tasks. Another new offering, Industry AI, will automate sector-specific workflows.

The report that SAP is preparing for job cuts doesn’t come as a complete surprise. Last week, Chief Financial Officer Dominik Asam told attendees of an investor event that the company expects its headcount to decline. Additionally, two of the software maker’s six directors will reportedly leave in connection with its shift to a more AI-centric strategy.

It’s unclear when the job cuts will take place. According to Bloomberg, SAP historically announced workforce reduction programs in January. The software maker took that route with its last major restructuring initiative, which saw it axe about 10,000 roles in 2024. The initiative cost about €3 billion.

The company said in a statement that “SAP continuously reviews its organization to ensure it remains aligned with its strategy and customer needs.”

#5329. Who should referee a national MLS, brokers or a neutral body?

The piece supports national listing standardization but opposes a broker-controlled system. It argues the operator should be neutral, like payment networks, to protect competition and limit reliance on private channels.  AI Summary

When Open Real Estate was announced, the question of a national listing system moved back to the center of our industry. I am early in my read on this particular initiative. But I have spent a long time on the underlying question, enough that I have written a white paper of more than 70 pages on why a broker-controlled national MLS is the wrong design and what a right one would look like. For the leaders reading this, I want to lay out the core of that thinking, because this is a decision our industry may actually make in the next few years, and we should make it with our eyes open.

First, credit where it is due. A coalition of large brokerages banded together and put their names to a public position. That takes coordination and conviction, and it is plainly a response to a real and growing trend, the migration of listings into private and exclusive channels that never touch the open market. The concern is legitimate. When inventory moves into walled gardens, buyers see less, agents compete on access instead of expertise, and the consumer is quietly disadvantaged. Leaders who are worried about that are worried about the right thing.

I see two problems, one practical and one structural, and the structural one is the one that should concern every leader who does not run one of the three or four largest firms in the country.

The practical problem is straightforward. The founders have said that Open Real Estate is not a national MLS and is not meant to replace local MLSs. Whatever we call it, it is built to function as shared national listing infrastructure, and that infrastructure includes a participant view option, where a listing can be seen only by agents at participating brokerages and cannot be publicly marketed by anyone. In other words, the model does not stop private listings. It gives them a larger, better-organized home. The exact behavior this is meant to counter can continue, and we have built a bigger shared system that still has walls inside it.

Consider the architecture we have now. Hundreds of local MLSs operate across the country. We complain about that fragmentation endlessly, and it does create real friction for agents and consumers. But the fragmentation also delivers a benefit almost no one names. Each MLS acts as its own silo, its own firewall. Because the data lives in hundreds of independent repositories, no single company controls the national market. There is a series called Silo that captures the idea well. Each silo runs itself, and no one can command the whole system. Our MLS structure has handed us that same protection almost by accident. The walls are inconvenient, and the walls are also the reason no one firm owns the country’s data.

Now collapse all of it into one national system, whatever label it carries, and ask the only question that matters. Who runs it? If the answer is that brokers run it, then the brokers with the deepest pockets will control the nation’s listing infrastructure. The independents, the single-office shops, the regional firms, they will have little to no voice. Whoever sits atop a broker-controlled national system writes the rules for everyone downstream, including their direct competitors. That is not a free market with shared plumbing. That is a tollgate owned by a few, and everyone else pays to pass through.

Powerfact: Whoever controls a national MLS controls the terms of competition for every agent in the country. That cannot be a competitor.

So, let me be clear that I am not against unification. A national MLS done correctly would be a real asset. It would let an agent see listings nationwide rather than stitching together access market by market. It would mean one playbook, the same rules, forms, and fields in every state, so practicing across state lines or relocating would not require relearning the mechanics each time. That consistency would benefitagents, brokers, and consumers. The debate should not be unify or do not unify. The fight is already here, and it should be about who holds the technology in the middle.

And we already have a proven answer inside our own economy. Visa and MasterCard.

The first bank card came from Bank of America. When other banks saw it working, each began building its own card and its own processing, and the result was chaos, because every bank set different rules and the consumer experience depended on which card you carried. The resolution was not to let the largest bank operate everyone else’s cards. It was Visa, a separate entity sitting in the middle. Each bank still runs its own business and competes on its own terms. The technology and the standards that make the system uniform for the consumer are handled by a neutral party that no single bank owns.

That is the template for a national MLS. Not control by the largest brokerages, but a neutral, broker-independent organization that operates the technology and maintains uniform rules, while every brokerage, large and small, continues to run its own business and compete on skill and service. Keep each firm a silo where it should be a silo. Make the shared rails in the middle belong to no one in particular. That is the only structure that stays fair to the smallest independent and the largest franchise at the same time.

When the next national platform is announced, and there will be more of them, do not evaluate it on the feature list. Evaluate it on governance. Ask who owns it, who sits on the board, how the rules get changed, and what recourse a small brokerage has if the controlling firms decide to change the terms. If the governance concentrates power in a handful of competitors, the convenience on the surface is not worth the dependency underneath. If the governance looks like Visa, neutral, independent, and accountable to all participants rather than to the biggest ones, then we may finally have something worth building.

I appreciate the effort behind Open Real Estate, and I share the concern that prompted it. But good intentions do not fix bad architecture. A national listing system run by brokers would trade the problem of private listings for the larger problem of a privatized commons, owned by the few and rented to the many. We can do better, and we have a model sitting in our wallets that shows us how. Build the referee first. Then build the league.

Darryl Davis, CSP, is a national speaker, real estate coach, and the bestselling author of How to Become a Power Agent® in Real Estate. Learn more at darrylspeaks.com.

#5328. Splendid Tianfu, Leisurely Sichuan: A Journey into the Ancient Culture of Bashu

BEIJING, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A news report from China Global Television Network Corporation:

From intangible cultural heritage experiences in the streets and alleys of ancient towns to the ancient Shu civilization showcased in museums, from everyday life in rural communities to ecological conservation in giant panda habitats, this year's "Splendid Tianfu â¢ Leisurely Sichuan" global cultural and tourism promotion project invited international youth from several countries to visit Sichuan. Through on-site visits, hands-on activities and face-to-face exchanges, they experienced the profound historical heritage and vibrant vitality of life in Sichuan. In the form of people-to-people cultural exchanges, the project promoted mutual learning among civilizations and presented to the world a credible, lovable and respectable image of Sichuan, China.

"Splendid Tianfu â¢ Leisurely Sichuan" is Sichuan Province's cultural and tourism brand. In June 2025, the Seventh Plenary Session of the 12th CPC Sichuan Provincial Committee called for efforts to develop the brand, using a distinctive regional identity to showcase Sichuan's natural beauty and cultural heritage and promote closer integration of culture and tourism.

"Splendid" evokes the fine craftsmanship of Shu brocade and Shu embroidery, as well as Sichuan's beautiful landscapes and long-standing cultural heritage. "Tianfu" carries the historical legacy of Sichuan. "Leisurely" captures the local people's love of life and their optimistic, easygoing outlook. It reflects a way of life that balances an enterprising spirit with a relaxed approach to life. From its landscapes to its everyday culture, the brand offers international visitors many ways to discover Sichuan.

The project focused on Three Kingdoms culture, Three-Su Culture, the ancient Shu civilization and giant panda conservation. It turned cultural resources into engaging experiences that visitors could take part in and share, bringing to life the natural beauty, cultural richness and everyday charm that the brand represents.

In the ancient town of Langzhong, the young visitors wandered through its historic streets, learned about Three Kingdoms culture and took part in traditional craft activities. Historical stories and traditional crafts came together, giving participants a chance to see how local traditions have been kept alive over the years.

In Zhongyan Village, Qingshen County, the guests explored sites linked to Three-Su Culture, sampled local food and chatted with residents. They saw how cultural traditions remain an integral part of everyday life in the village, and how they continue to be shared from one generation to the next.

In Guanghan, the Sanxingdui Museum and the Sanxing Village Archaeological Exploration Base introduced the young visitors to the ancient Shu civilization. They appreciated ancient artifacts, tried making bronze objects and took part in simulated archaeological excavations. They also asked questions and shared their thoughts as they explored this ancient civilization. Among the visitors were Anna and Ye Zimu, two international students from Russia, who saw the Bronze Sacred Tree at the Sanxingdui Museum and tried their hand at bronze casting. They said the artifacts at Sanxingdui were unlike anything they had seen before. Making bronze objects themselves gave them a firsthand experience of this ancient civilization, and they hoped to take their creations back to Russia as gifts for their families. Anna also said she was impressed by how Chinese museums bring history and culture together in their exhibitions.

In Dayi County, the guests visited the Dasuanping Protection Station in Giant Panda National Park to learn about local conservation efforts. They also visited Taiping Community in Xieyuan, where they tried traditional bamboo weaving and observed everyday community life. Together, these experiences offered visitors another perspective on Sichuan, showing how ecological conservation and rural development can go hand in hand.

Su Zhiyao, an international student studying in China, accompanied park staff to the protection station. In the mountain forest at an altitude of 2,140 meters, she watched real-time footage from infrared cameras to observe giant pandas moving in the wild. She said that visiting pandas in their natural habitat and using infrared camera footage to observe their activities gave her a more direct understanding of how people and nature can live in harmony.

The visitors' experiences were also featured in television programs and short videos, which followed them as they took part in activities and shared their experiences. The programs are being released across different platforms, with content precisely targeted to different platforms and audiences.

From ancient towns to rural communities, and from cultural heritage to ecological conservation, "Splendid Tianfu â¢ Leisurely Sichuan" continues to send invitations to the world, inviting friends from around the world to visit Sichuan and understand Sichuan. By building bridges for cross-cultural communication through face-to-face dialogue between people, it enhances understanding in encounters among civilizations, shares development achievements and a better life, and continues to tell vivid and lively Bashu stories overseas.

#5326. Will the Anthropic IPO supercharge San Francisco’s already-hot housing market?

Anthropic’s $1.5T IPO adds a new source of liquidity to San Francisco, where the median single-family price rose 29% year over year to $2.39M and 86% of homes sold above asking. With fewer than 700 listings, additional demand could intensify competition, even as tech shares remain volatile.  AI Summary

On Nov. 19, Anthropic went public on Nasdaq at a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion, creating perhaps 5000 millionaires, many of whom reside in the city of San Francisco, where the company is based.

The question people keep asking me is: what happens to the real estate market in San Francisco?

San Francisco’s housing market was already the hottest market in the country before Anthropic’s IPO came to town. While the rest of the country wrestled with mortgage rates near multi-decade highs, San Francisco faced bidding wars and intense competition. The median single-family home sale price rose 29% year over year to $2.39 million in October, the largest gain since February 2018. Some 86% of homes sold above asking price, up from 77% a year earlier.

Among 552 U.S. counties with at least 300 single-family home sales from August through October, San Francisco was the only one where prices rose more than 10%. The typical county saw prices rise just 1.9%, 149 counties recorded declines, and San Francisco homes were more than four times as likely as the typical U.S. home to sell above asking.

In past decades, a single or even a series of IPOs have not notably been a driver of the San Francisco housing market. Macro market cycles have mattered more. Notably, San Francisco home prices tend to follow the peaks and valleys of the entire Nasdaq Composite by about 9-12 months. This makes sense since any one IPO might impact the wealth of a few hundred people, where the Nasdaq represents an entire universe of tech related wealth and economic dynamism.

Compass market analyst Janel Evans-Anderson looked at 19 major tech IPOs over the last 20+ years and notes that IPOs from companies like Google, Facebook and Uber might spur some home sales, but much more important are the big trends in tech and the economy.

But the scale of the Anthropic IPO, combined with San Francisco’s current housing market conditions, creates a different set of circumstances from previous technology IPOs.

The economic effects of Anthropic’s IPO may have already hit San Francisco real estate, even before employees can access the full value of their shares.

In the past, the IPO was a starting point for growth and wealth creation. Now the IPO may be the exit. For example, NVIDIA went public in 1999, but the massive wealth created by the company happened nearly 20 years later. Anthropic’s IPO valuation is 100x or 1000x the old thresholds.

Employees of Anthropic and other highly-valued tech firms have access to capital in ways that were not available to tech workers 10 or 20 years ago. In the last decade, a robust secondary market for private company stock has developed. Many executives at hot AI companies (not just Anthropic) have been able to sell their shares into the secondary market for years prior to the IPO.

Equity-rich tech workers can also borrow against their shares. This financial instrument lets people access the cash, pay cash for a house, and not have to pay taxes on the sale of the stock. In decades past, when a big IPO was $1 billion, perhaps one or two execs at the startup would have access to this kind of borrowing. When the IPO is $1 trillion, suddenly hundreds or thousands of employees have access to capital prior to the IPO.

Anthropic’s IPO is introducing an enormous pool of newly liquid wealth into a housing market where prices are already rising rapidly and available homes are scarce. And because Anthropic employees face lockup restrictions, with sales limited initially to 10% of holdings and more shares unlocking through 2027, that wealth could keep reaching the housing market well into 2027.

San Francisco County was already the hottest housing market in the nation before the IPO. Among 552 U.S. counties with at least 300 single-family home sales from August through October, it was the only one where prices rose more than 10%. The typical county saw prices rise just 1.9%, while 149 counties recorded declines. Homes in San Francisco County were over four times more likely to sell for above their asking price than the typical U.S. home.

It’s not just that the IPOs are bigger now. This cash tsunami floods into a housing market that is much smaller than it used to be. There are fewer than 700 single family homes and condos for sale in the city as of the end of November 2026. That’s about 20% fewer than normal for the 2010s and is 40% fewer than in 2012 when Facebook IPO’d.

When new purchasing power enters a market with limited inventory, competition intensifies and pushes prices higher. The imbalance is particularly striking in 2026: we’ve counted over 250 sales in the city this year that closed at least $1 million over asking.

The days since the IPO have been dramatically volatile for Anthropic shares and for the entire market. Valuations of many public tech companies have been hit by market turmoil in recent weeks. It could be that by next spring the AI bubble has popped and much of this wealth has evaporated.

Looking back on the dot-com bubble burst in 2000, that led to a sharp change in the housing market in the city. Annual home price appreciation plummeted from nearly 30% per year at the peak of the bubble to 0%. At the time, a handful of executives that had borrowed against their shares had to sell the home to pay back the loan. If the Anthropic IPO is 1000x bigger than previous events, what does a bubble burst look like this time?

#5325. Binance Secures In-Principle Approval in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Plans Asia Hub in Bhutan

The regulatory milestone marks a major step toward Binance establishing an Asia hub in Gelephu Mindfulness City, alongside commitments to create jobs and strengthen Bhutan's digital-asset capabilities

BANGKOK, Nov. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Binance, the leading global financial platform powered by blockchain, has received in-principle approval (IPA) from the Gelephu Central Bank (GCB) to establish regulated digital-asset operations in Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC), Bhutan.

The milestone was marked at Binance Blockchain Week 2026, where Binance and GMC signed a cooperation agreement setting out their broader partnership and plans for GMC to become an Asia hub for Binance users. The IPA is an important milestone in a broader, ongoing effort to expand access and build out the ecosystem locally. Binance has been deepening its presence in Bhutan since launching a national crypto-powered tourism payment system in 2025. As the partnership progresses, Binance will continue building out the local digital-asset ecosystem.

Binance will now work with GCB to fulfil the conditions attached to the IPA and complete the remaining regulatory requirements before receiving its full licence.

The partnership goes beyond licensing. Binance plans to establish a substantive operational presence in Bhutan, creating employment opportunities while investing in the development of talent and digital-asset capabilities.

As part of the partnership, Binance will work with GMC to build capabilities and upskill the talent pool, including through employment, training, knowledge sharing and collaboration across areas such as digital assets, compliance and operations. The parties also intend to explore opportunities to develop GMC as a regional centre of excellence, supporting Binance's broader operations in Asia while building expertise and capabilities within GMC.

Speaking on this milestone, Jigdrel Singay, Board Director of Gelephu Mindfulness City, said "Binance choosing Gelephu Mindfulness City as a base for its Asia operations is an important milestone for what we are building in Bhutan. Our ambition is not simply to attract global companies to establish an entity here. We want them to build real operations, create meaningful jobs, develop talent and transfer capabilities that remain in the country over the long term.

"The in-principle approval is an important first step, and we look forward to working closely with Binance and GCB as Binance completes the remaining regulatory requirements and builds its presence in GMC," Singay added.

SB Seker Head of APAC, Binance said, "Establishing an Asia hub in Gelephu Mindfulness City is a strategic decision that reflects Binance's commitment to operating within clear, progressive regulatory frameworks. The IPA from GCB is an important validation of GMC's approach to digital asset regulation, one that protects users while enabling innovation."

"GMC's vision of combining traditional values with cutting-edge technology, powered by renewable energy, makes it an ideal location for Binance's regional center of excellence. We are committed to making this partnership a model for responsible growth in the digital asset sector," added Seker.

The partnership forms part of GMC's broader ambition to establish Bhutan as a trusted and internationally connected hub for digital assets and financial innovation, combining a clear regulatory framework with a long-term focus on developing local talent and institutional capabilities.

The granting of the IPA does not constitute a full licence. Binance must satisfy the conditions specified by GCB and complete the remaining regulatory requirements before the relevant regulated activities may commence.

For more information, visit www.gmc.bt.

Beyond financial services, its ecosystem extends to education, research, social impact, institutional solutions and Web3 innovation. #5324. AI vs. housing: A battle for the direction of mortgage rates in 2027

Volatility tied to the stock market and Fed policy has made the spreads widen from the lows of the year. This has kept mortgage rates above 7% as the lowest spreads of 2026 would have rates under 7% today.  AI Summary

As Thanksgiving week ends, clear battle lines have been drawn between AI and the housing market. The Federal Reserve has emphatically told the marketplace that not only has AI not been disinflationary as some people have feared — with massive unemployment and huge productivity gains — but that it is the aspect of the economy that is overheating, along with tariffs and the conflict in Iran. So as you can imagine when AI stocks were selling off and bond yields were falling recently, that lays the groundwork for a battle between AI and housing and where mortgage rates can go.

In the 2026 HousingWire forecast, I anticipated the following ranges:

One thing about the last two weeks: the economic data was fine, jobless claims were low, GDP grew over 4% and we haven’t seen any real weakness in consumption data. In any normal situation, bond yields and rates would have stayed steady or risen. However, the AI stock sell-off was massive and spooked a lot people, including those in the White House.As I have discussed often on the HousingWire Daily podcast, AI companies are now showing weakness. If the AI sector takes a lot of damage in 2027, that can prompt the Fed to end its rate-hike cycle — although we also need to resolve the Iran conflict and limit tariff damage. I believe that no matter what actually happened in the second half of this year, the Fed was bent on getting back its “insurance” rate cuts from last year, which means we have two more rate hikes left. However, the rate-hike cycle can stop there if the AI slowdown is legit.

Another key with AI is you’re starting to see a lot of credit deterioration in AI companies. That can change the conversation to a real slowdown where the Fed might get a bit more dovish. You can see the stock sell-off spooked the White House so much that they got involved and tried to stop the bleeding.For myself, I am keeping track of the CoreWeave stock price and their credit rating, because if the credit markets gets worse for smaller AI companies, that can be bullish for mortgage rates in 2027. If we can resolve the Iran conflict, end tariffs and get an AI slowdown — that will make the Fed sound less hawkish for sure. As you can see in the chart below, the 10-year yield has stopped heading higher, but is putting up a big fight right now on which direction to go next.

Mortgage spreads have recently gotten worse, which is a big variable in why rates got as high as 7.60% recently. We need less volatility in the bond and stock markets for spreads to get back toward 2%. In fact, the way spreads are acting right now is very normal; their job is to compress volatility with mortgage rates, and when yields make an aggressive move lower from the big run-up, the spreads do get worse. To get sub-7 % rates again, we need the 10-year yield under 4.85% and mortgage spreads back toward 2%.

Historically, mortgage spreads have ranged from 1.60% to 1.80%. Last week, spreads rose to 2.31% from 2.18% a week earlier.

Let’s compare last week’s mortgage rates to where they would be at this year’s best spread levels and the worst levels of this cycle.

Note: It’s Thanksgiving week, which, like all holidays, destroys the weekly housing data lines, but Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year’s are the big ones. So, take this week’s data with a grain of salt, as you should take next week’s data too. We only have a few weeks left of legit weekly housing data until Christmas and New Year’s take their toll, and we are getting ready for 2027.

Our pending home sales data provides a week-to-week perspective, though holidays and short-term fluctuations can affect results. This weekly pending sales data typically takes 30-60 days to reflect in sales data.

Housing data has stabilized with rates moving a tad lower; two weeks ago we saw slight growth. I would chalk this up to a stabilization coming after some real weakness, when mortgage rates shot up from 6.75% to 7.60%. We are in the traditional seasonal decline in our weekly data, and saw the typical week-to-week hit in demand due to the holidays. Of course, the year-over-year is worse than last year at this time because mortgage rates were heading toward 6%.Here are the pending sales for last week over the last two years:

Purchase application data, which looks out 30-90 days, has softened as mortgage rates rose above 6.64%  and headed toward 7.60%. However, in the last few weeks, just like our weekly pending home sales data, purchase application data has improved. Last week we saw a 10% gain from week to week; this data line is from two weeks ago, not the Thanksgiving week. Just be mindful this is a trend survey data line, and the percentage movement can be wild from week to week. From what I see, purchase apps recently are showing more stabilization than real growth.

Here are the stats on purchase apps so far in 2026:

Housing inventory declined slightly last week and is in its seasonal decline for 2026, as the peak in inventory has already occurred. Inventory growth picked up when mortgage rates headed toward 7.60%; before that, inventory growth was slow this year, and we even had some weeks when year-over-year inventory was negative. Until mid-June, it was hard for the comps to show growth this year but now that’s much easier as housing demand was heading toward a nine-month high last year this time.

We are heading toward the end of the year, when new listings typically fall to the yearly low. One concern with higher rates is that some sellers may decide not to put their homes on the market; that hasn’t happened this year, even with rates as high as 7.60%. Since most sellers are buyers, this is a positive sign. Even with elevated rates, 2026 has been the best new listings year since 2022; we had a few weeks of over 80,000 during the seasonal peak months.In a normal environment, new listings range from 80,000 to 100,000 per week during peak periods. For context, during the housing bubble years, new listings ranged from 250,000 to 400,000 per week for several years.Here is last week’s new listings data for the past two years:

Typically, about one-third of homes see price reductions before they sell, reflecting the housing market’s dynamic nature. Overall, price-cut percentages this year have been lower than last year. This held true until rates moved above 6.64% and then headed toward 7.60%. At that point, demand fell, and the year-over-year price-cut percentage rose 1%, and last week the year-over-year price-cut gap was 1% higher than last year. Last year, of course, rates were lower and demand was picking up. However, even last year, prices weren’t growing much either.In my 2026 home-price forecast, I called for a national decline of -0.62% for the year. Home-price growth really isn’t going anywhere this year, and my -0.62% forecast looks impossible now as we simply don’t have enough time left in the year to get prices down enough for that forecast to be correct. For months Case Shiller, which lags our data, was still running at 2.1% year over year and FHFA was running at 2.5% in the recent reports.

Just remember, looking at the history of home prices from 1942-2026, it’s rare to have nominal national price declines. If you take 2007-2011 out of the data pool, we actually never had a year of 1% decline even with 13 recession since WWII. In 1990, home prices were down -0.7% and in 1991 it was down 0.2%.The price-cut percentage for last week:

It’s jobs week again and the recent jobs data is still looking good enough for economic expansion. We might not get the seasonal hiring boost like we did last month, but jobless claims data is still very low.

We also want to keep an eye out on AI stocks and the bond market, yields did go higher last week when AI stocks started to come off their lows. Of course keep an eye out on any headlines about the Iran conflict or the trade war. Soon the Democrats will take over Congress so we will have a different set of political variables next year, but this is the last month in a crazy year and we have no shortage of drama events that can move rates.

#5323. Binance Pay, DK Bank and Tether Sign MOU to Expand Stablecoin Payments to Merchants Across Bhutan, Starting with USD₮

Signed at Binance Blockchain Week 2026, the initiative builds on Bhutan's national crypto payment network and plans incentives to help merchants adopt stablecoin payments

BANGKOK, Nov. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Binance Pay, DK Bank, Gelephu Mindfulness City's official bank, and Tether today signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to bring stablecoin payments to merchants across Bhutan, starting with USDâ®. The MOU was signed at Binance Blockchain Week Bangkok 2026 by Thomas Gregory, Vice President of Payments & Fiat at Binance; Ugyen Tenzin, Chief Executive Officer of DK Bank; and Tether.

The MOU builds on the payment network Binance Pay and DK Bank launched in May 2025, when Bhutan became the first country to introduce a national-level crypto payment system for tourism. Subject to eligibility requirements, users can pay participating merchants with supported digital assets, and merchants receive Bhutanese ngultrum. More than 3,700 merchants now accept payments through the system, from hotels and airlines to roadside vendors.

Under the MOU, the parties will work to promote stablecoin payments for merchants on this network.

To encourage participation, eligible users can receive a 5% rebate on qualifying transactions, capped at US$5 per transaction. Eligibility criteria and final terms are subject to agreement.

"Bhutan has shown that crypto payments can work at a national level," said Thomas Gregory, VP of Payments & Fiat, Binance. "With Tether and DK Bank, we want to make stablecoins and crypto the easier way to pay in Bhutan, and make accepting it worth it for every merchant."

"Since 2025, Bhutanese merchants have shown growing interest in accepting digital payments," said Ugyen Tenzin, CEO of DK Bank. "This initiative further enhances their ability to accept payments from international customers, and merchants can benefit from the reach of digital payment networks while continuing to receive their payments entirely in local currency."

The MOU is non-binding. Implementation, including the launch date and rebate terms, remains subject to final agreement between the parties.

#5322. Jensen Huang returns, but controversies keep growing around Nvidia

THIS WEEK IN ENTERPRISE by Robert Hof

Jensen Huang’s back, and not everyone is happy with that.

Nvidia’s board reversed the resignation of its former and current-again CEO Monday, apparently under pressure from the well-known business genius and lame-duck President Donald Trump, who worried that the stock market and the AI trade would suffer without him at the helm.

Huang (pictured) clearly has management talent, having built one of the most valuable companies in the world. But his return, amid continuing revelations and questions about Nvidia’s business, sets an awful precedent in business. No one person should be too important to fail, and Huang set up a corporate structure that courts disaster if he’s forced to leave again or gets run over by a bus. That’s a world-class failure of a CEO and his board at one of their most basic jobs, and his tech-bro enablers should know better than to clamor for his return.

After all, internal and government investigations continue, as more details come to light about probably the worst of the whole affair(s). It’s clear that at a time when there’s existential worry about China closing the U.S. lead in AI — a potential defense and cybersecurity disaster — the chief supplier of AI chips was allowing cutting-edge chips to be sent to China. (Thankfully, that loophole may be about to close.) Oh, and this week’s stock market pretty much discounted much of the supposed benefit Huang’s reinstatement was supposed to provide.

So what are we left with? The CEO of the pivotal company in AI is back with not even a slap on the wrist, let alone any consequences for multiple affairs — one with a woman who shuttled both barred GPUs and apparently inside information to China, another with an Nvidia VP, plus at least a couple others he fessed up to. Oh, and he lied about them until he couldn’t anymore. Any semblance of corporate governance and ethics — at Nvidia and everywhere else by example — is utterly torched.

Hey, if you think that’s a buying opportunity, I’ve got some high-end GPUs in Singapore to sell you. Anyway, let’s move on before I tell you what I really think.

Paul Gillin dove into why open-weight AI models that enterprises can tailor to their specific needs are taking off this year. “The shift toward open-weight models represents a permanent maturation of enterprise IT from experimentation to disciplined financial and architectural management,” he notes. “Success is no longer about raw model parameter size or benchmark ranking, but matching the model to the task.”

Last week Palo Alto Networks said it will acquire Applied Compute for $4.5 billion. This week was CrowdStrike’s turn, as it pulled the trigger on buying Zscaler for a pretty stunning $44 billion. As AI makes cyberattacks far easier and more numerous, it seems a sure bet that today’s rickety cybersecurity industry with hundred of point products won’t stand.

AI continues to be a big driver of upside earnings surprises, but investors increasingly wary of AI spending are all over the place. Dell in particular more than doubled its revenue, only to see its shares go nowhere Wednesday, while HP got hit by the PC slowdown but saw its shares rise more than 12%. Likewise, HPE’s stock slid despite an upbeat forecast.

Next week, look for earnings from Salesforce, Snowflake, UiPath, Marvell, MongoDB, NetApp, Okta and more.

But the big news next week will be AWS re:Invent, which customarily releases dozens of new services at its re:Invent conference in Las Vegas. SiliconANGLE, theCUBE Research, theCUBE, along with tens of thousands of attendees, will be onsite and we’ll have all the news, analysis and interviews.

#5321. KuCoin Advances Australian Engagement at CryptoCon Sydney, Spotlighting Global Infrastructure and Local Accountability

SYDNEY, Nov. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- KuCoin highlighted the importance of connecting global exchange capabilities with local responsibilities at CryptoCon Sydney at ICC Sydney. During the panel "Global Infrastructure, Local Accountability: Where Exchanges Fit in Crypto's Next Phase," KuCoin CMO Skylar W and Managing Director of KuCoin in Australia James Pinch discussed how exchanges can respond to broader financial needs through infrastructure investment, market-specific governance and local delivery. They were joined by Zach Ahmajani, Head of Operations at KuCoin in Australia, in a discussion moderated by Lydia Ward, Growth Manager of KuCoin in Australia.

Skylar described an industry in which trading volume, liquidity and asset selection remain important, but expectations increasingly extend to the infrastructure and operating standards behind those services. She connected KuCoin's investment in security and transparency through its $2 Billion Trust Project with the development of its global compliance framework and institutional services. "Global capabilities are the starting point. What matters is how the product works locally, with clear responsibilities from day one," said Skylar W. Her remarks also highlighted continued work on trading architecture and security infrastructure to support performance and resilience as financial activity becomes more demanding.

During the discussion, Skylar also introduced KuCoin 5.0 as an example of how those investments translate into tangible improvements for users. Launched under the "Trust, Built-in." initiative, the platform-wide upgrade offers distinct Lite and Pro experiences and a single point of access to AI assistance across the platform. It also introduces a Unified Trading Account that allows eligible users at VIP1 and above to manage funds and trade across spot, margin and futures from one account.

James brought that discussion back to the tasks users need to complete. Drawing on a focus group involving people who had purchased crypto in the previous 12 to 24 months, he described participants using digital assets to pay vendors and send money overseas. Building on its collaboration with the convention in 2025, its three-year partnership with CryptoCon Sydney provides an ongoing forum for engagement with Australian users and industry partners. Together with its Sydney office and local leadership team established in 2025, the partnership supports KuCoin's long-term approach to bringing global resources into services shaped by local expertise and needs.

#5320. Entrepreneurship Trends (2026): Registered Agents Inc Examines What New Business Formation Data Reveals by Consumer365

NEW YORK, Nov. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Consumer365 has recognized Registered Agents Inc for its Business Formation Report, a monthly resource providing insight into U.S. entrepreneurship trends through state-level business registration data and analysis of changing formation activity.

The October 2026 findings reveal continued growth in new business creation across the country, with 576,818 new formations recorded during the month. The figure represents the highest October total on record and extends a broader pattern of year-over-year growth throughout 2026.

The report offers insight into how entrepreneurship is evolving across the United States. By tracking new entity filings across all 50 states and Washington, D.C., Registered Agents Inc provides data that helps economists, policymakers, journalists and business stakeholders examine changes in entrepreneurial activity.

Business Formation Activity Continues to Grow

According to the October 2026 report, approximately 5.9 million new business entities had been formed nationwide through October. The total represented a 16% increase compared with the same period in 2025.

October alone recorded 576,818 formations, exceeding the previous October high of 532,545 established in 2025. Month-over-month activity increased by nearly 4%, indicating that formation levels remained strong enough to maintain an elevated position.

New business registrations can provide an early indication of economic activity and entrepreneurial confidence. Establishing a legal entity is often an important step for individuals pursuing independent business ventures, formalizing commercial activities or entering new markets.

Regional Differences Highlight Changes in Entrepreneurship

The October report demonstrates how formation activity varies across individual states.

Florida recorded 62,687 new formations, while Texas registered 46,446 and California reported 41,156. Delaware recorded 32,193 formations, followed by Wyoming with 25,935.

October's year-over-year growth highlighted strong momentum across several states beyond the largest formation markets. Colorado led the nation with a 46.7% increase, followed by Kentucky at 38.7% and Louisiana at 34.9%. Missouri also maintained strong growth at 32.6%, while Mississippi and Tennessee recorded increases of 31.3% and 30.6%, respectively.

These figures illustrate why geographic analysis is important when examining business creation. States with large registration totals may not necessarily experience the fastest growth. Meanwhile, jurisdictions with smaller formation volumes can demonstrate significant changes in entrepreneurial activity.

Several factors may influence regional patterns, including population changes, operating costs, tax policies, regulatory environments and local economic conditions. Missouri's increase, for example, coincided with changes to state capital gains taxation.

Business Owner Sentiment Offers Further Insight

The Business Formation Report also includes survey findings that provide additional context about the experiences and expectations of existing business owners.

In the October 2026 survey, 48% of respondents described their businesses as stronger than a year earlier. Twenty-eight percent reported relatively unchanged conditions, while 24% said business conditions had weakened.

Expectations for the coming year were also notable. Fifty-nine percent of surveyed business owners said they were very optimistic about their businesses' prospects over the next 12 months. Another 23% reported neutral expectations, while 18% were not optimistic.

The survey also examined how uncertainty surrounding the November elections was influencing customers' willingness to do business. More than one-third of respondents (36%) reported no meaningful changes in customer behavior. However, 25% said customers were more hesitant to commit, while 17% reported requests for greater flexibility. On the other hand, 13% said customers were accelerating purchasing decisions, and 9% reported increased willingness to purchase.

These findings provide a broader perspective on entrepreneurship beyond the number of newly registered entities. Formation totals indicate the pace of business creation, while survey responses offer insight into how existing business owners assess current conditions and prepare for future demand.

A Monthly Resource for Tracking U.S. Entrepreneurship

Registered Agents Inc publishes its Business Formation Report on the second Tuesday of each month, covering the previous month's activity.

The report tracks new entity filings across all 50 states and Washington, D.C. The company states that formation data is cross-referenced with U.S. Census data and information from Secretaries of State or equivalent agencies.

Monthly reporting allows readers to examine formation totals, compare year-over-year changes and identify regional developments. The information is made available to economists, journalists, policymakers, entrepreneurs and industry stakeholders interested in understanding the business formation environment.

Registered Agents Inc helps entrepreneurs establish and maintain businesses through services that include professional websites, domains, business addresses and phone numbers. The company aims to make legitimate business formation and professional business establishment more accessible to entrepreneurs from different backgrounds.

As business creation continues to evolve, consistent reporting can help distinguish broader economic patterns from short-term fluctuations. The October 2026 findings provide a current view of national formation activity, regional growth and business-owner sentiment.

#5317. Hackers reportedly breach key US Air Force cloud platform

Hackers have reportedly breached Cloud One, a platform that the U.S. Air Force uses to power dozens of internal applications.

Reuters broke the news today, citing three people familiar with the matter. The news agency reported that the cyberattack could “jeopardize a vast swath” of sensitive data.

Cloud One runs on infrastructure from Amazon.com Inc., Microsoft Corp., Oracle Corp. and Google LLC. The applications that it powers perform a wide range of tasks. Some are designed to ease administrative chores such as managing personnel records, while others analyze radar data and track the location of hardware assets.

The breach was reportedly discovered “within the past month or so.” Technical personnel spotted malicious activity while performing a system upgrade. According to Reuters, the investigators probing the incident have asked the U.S. Cyber Command to assist with the analysis.

Many key details about the cyberattack, including when it started, remain unclear. However, today’s report did specify that the breach saw hackers gain access to Cloud One’s control plane.

A control plane is a software engine that coordinates a technology system’s other components. Its role varies based on the system that it powers. The Kubernetes control plane, for example, performs tasks such as spinning up containers, while a network’s control plane coordinates the flow of traffic.

Reuters’ sources said that the Cloud One control plane can theoretically be used to check the operational status of Air Force assets. However, it’s unclear whether hackers stole any sensitive data.

The attackers reportedly compromised Cloud One via a software vulnerability. The report didn’t specify whether the flaw was in a custom software component or an external, off-the-shelf product. In the latter scenario, other organizations that use the off-the-shelf product may also be vulnerable.

Hackers often chain together multiple vulnerabilities rather than relying on a single flaw. Additionally, they’re increasingly using artificial intelligence to speed up cyberattacks.

Earlier this week, the New York Times reported that a threat actor had breached a data analysis system used by the U.S. intelligence community. The hackers used an open-source AI cyberattack tool called ARTEX. The breach reportedly didn’t compromise any classified data.

According to Reuters, the Air Force has paused an internal project focused on moving legacy applications to Cloud One. It also blocked updates to workloads that already run on the platform. That left personnel unable to patch applications against a “new batch of serious software vulnerabilities.” The report suggests that the vulnerabilities were in off-the-shelf software that is also used by other organizations.

The Cloud One hack and the recent ARTEX-powered breach continue a string of recent cyberattacks against the federal government. Earlier this week, the U.S. Treasury Department reportedly took parts of its infrastructure offline in response to a cyber incident. A few days earlier, sources told NBC News reported that hackers had breached a payment system used by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

#5315. So you got a Microsoft Voluntary Exit Offer? Here’s what to do next

by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm

Nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn. This is the fourth post in his series on “Life after Big Tech,” including the Seattle startup guide, laid off at 50 and VC funding is changing dramatically.

Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a big decision to make in the next few weeks: take the company’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.

Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the initiative in a memo on Oct. 26: a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) for about 60,000 employees at level 70 and below, which includes general managers and some vice presidents, in the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and India. That’s roughly 27% of Microsoft’s 223,000 people. The company expects 3,000 or fewer of them to accept.

Microsoft says the terms match its standard severance: base pay tied to level and tenure, continued stock vesting, a period of health coverage and career transition help. The severance package varies greatly based on the seniority or level of the employee and the number of years of service. Employees have until early December to decide and would leave by the end of the year.

The offer follows the Voluntary Retirement Program (VRP) that Microsoft extended to about 8,750 U.S. employees in April. About 30% of them, or roughly 2,600 people, took that offer.

All of this comes as Microsoft cuts jobs and changes the kinds of roles it hires for, while pouring money into AI infrastructure and data centers. At the same time, AI is reshaping the broader workforce, flattening management layers and changing what employers look for in new hires.

The worry I hear most is whether more layoffs are waiting on the other side. So the real choice is whether you leave on your own terms or let the company decide for you.

I hear two questions from Microsoft employees thinking about the VEO: How easily can I get another job, and how hard is it to start a company right now?

Harder than you think, and it depends a lot on who you are. We are in the “low hire, low fire” economy.

There is MASSIVE demand for AI-native builders — product managers, data scientists and engineers — as companies adapt products to deal with AI. Companies are also in the process of adopting AI.

One of the fastest-growing tech roles is the “Forward Deployed Engineer,” who implements AI solutions at customers. Security is also job #1 as models and agents get smarter and better at hacking legacy systems.

But it is very hard to be seen by recruiters and hiring managers right now. Candidates are using AI to customize their resumes to each job and using AI agents to apply, sending out 100 to 200 job applications per day. Recruiters are inundated with resumes and job applications, many of which are fake or inappropriate for the role.

It is critical to leverage your network in the job search, which can be hard if you have spent your entire career within one company.

“It has never been easier to build a product, and it has rarely been harder to fund a company.”

Hiring managers have changed what they look for, too. AI fluency is becoming table stakes. The “process” of how you build/sell/market with AI is more important than what you build. Candidates are expected to show prototypes and proof of how they use AI tools every day.

The jobs themselves are changing. A friend told me last month that he wanted an engineering manager role. There are fewer manager roles in the market now.

AI has driven a reduction in management layers and a general flattening of organizations. The engineering team at a small AI company today is a CTO and a group of strong individual contributors. It is normal for managers to have 10 to 30 direct reports now, versus five to 10 in the pre-AI era.

Product management, program management and design teams are shrinking, as well, as AI automates certain jobs.

Hiring managers may view spending your whole career at Microsoft as a yellow flag. Microsoft is an iconic but unusual company. Almost no one else sells to and services customers the way Microsoft does, with an account executive inside nearly every large enterprise in the world.

The skills that get you promoted in Redmond don’t always carry over to a 500- to 5,000-person software company.

It has never been easier to build a product, and it has rarely been harder to fund a company.

Software is cheap to build now. A product leader and an engineer using AI tools can ship in weeks what used to take a team a year.

This cuts both ways for startups. Every good idea attracts a dozen competitors within months, and the big platforms will copy anything that works.

The true strength of a startup today is the ability to grow revenue quickly and establish leadership in a beachhead market. The sales, marketing, product-led growth and distribution strategies are becoming the most critical parts of the business.

The bar for venture funding is extremely high. Jason Lemkin of SaaStr recently shared data from ICONIQ showing that top “AI forward” startups under $10 million in annual recurring revenue are growing 900% a year at the median.

One venture investor told me they advise their portfolio companies that if they aren’t on track for a $10 million run rate within two years, they won’t raise another round. Last week I spoke with an investor who owns part of a business with $4 million in revenue, growing 100% a year and losing $1 million, and it can’t raise.

1) Think VERY big, raise a lot and grow fast enough to justify it. Build an incredible team pursuing an ambitious idea. Raise a large round based on the promise of becoming the next Anthropic, OpenAI or legal AI startup Harvey. Many of the most interesting companies are not software or AI-related, but are “deep tech” companies in defense, robotics, energy and biotech.

2) Raise a moderate amount of money from angels, family offices and nontraditional funds to build a business that has the ability to be profitable on one round of financing. You can control your destiny by building a company that doesn’t rely on the venture capital funding market.

3) Bootstrap and build a business that you own. Fund it yourself, grow it with revenue and get to profitability.

The question that most people are NOT asking is: What do I really want?

Before December, block out an afternoon and think about the last time you were happy at work.

There are many frameworks for figuring out what you want in your career and life in general. I’m a fan of the Four Elements exercise. Write down three times in your career when you felt energized and effective. From those, work out what gives you energy, where you have the most impact, what culture you do best in and what your constraints are: money, kids, aging parents and how many more years you want to work.

On LinkedIn, I have seen examples of Microsoft employees taking the VEO to start their own businesses in property management, buy car washes, take time to recharge, spend time with family and travel.

Other employees are starting the job search in earnest but not taking the VEO. Many others are just getting back to work and doubling down on Microsoft.

Whichever way you go, start now. Start by aligning on your priorities and what you want from your career. If you stay, use the next year to build your skills with AI and to grow a network outside Redmond. If you leave to build something, decide early which of the three funding paths you’re on, because that choice shapes everything that follows.

The people I’ve watched land well after Big Tech had one thing in common: they knew what they wanted before they walked out the door, whether that was a new role, a company of their own or a year with their family.

MediaTek powers more than two billion devices every year, from the most advanced AI infrastructure on the planet to the everyday devices that make life smarter, faster, and more connected. For everyone. MediaTek silicon is the common thread running through all of it. Yeah, MediaTek does that.
